nodes.label: BuildBetter Agent Instructions (Project Overview)
nodes.rationale: Defines BuildBetter as a full-stack PC upgrade recommendation website that must estimate PC value, identify bottlenecks, recommend upgrades, and work even without real API keys via mock pricing and rule-based explanations.

nodes.label: Phase 1 - Clean Current Frontend
nodes.rationale: Fix syntax errors, broken JSX, dead code, and styling issues so the app renders without errors before further feature work.

nodes.label: Phase 2 - Split Frontend Into Components
nodes.rationale: Refactor App.jsx into smaller components (Hero, StepCard, SpecsForm, etc.) to keep the project understandable for a beginner.

nodes.label: Phase 3 - Add System Info Auto-Fill
nodes.rationale: Add an Auto-Fill From System Info feature so users can paste Windows System Information text and have fields filled automatically.

nodes.label: Phase 4 - Build Backend
nodes.rationale: Create a Node/Express JavaScript backend (no TypeScript) running on port 5000 with dotenv and cors.

nodes.label: Phase 6 - Real Pricing API Plan
nodes.rationale: Defines provider priority: Best Buy for real new-part pricing, eBay for used pricing, OpenAI for explanations, Amazon Creators API as future-optional; app must work with no real keys.

nodes.label: Phase 7 - Pricing Service Structure
nodes.rationale: pricingService.js should read PRICING_PROVIDER, call the selected provider, normalize results, and fall back to mock pricing on missing credentials or request failure.

nodes.label: Phase 8 - Best Buy Provider
nodes.rationale: Best Buy is the main real-pricing provider using the Best Buy Products API; falls back to mock pricing if BESTBUY_API_KEY is missing.

nodes.label: Phase 9 - eBay Provider
nodes.rationale: Uses eBay Browse API for used-market pricing to estimate current used value; falls back to mock pricing on failure or missing credentials.

nodes.label: Phase 10 - Amazon Future Provider
nodes.rationale: Amazon Product Advertising API is deprecated, so Amazon support is scoped to optional future scaffolding (amazonCreatorsProvider.js) and must never block the MVP.

nodes.label: Phase 11 - OpenAI API Service
nodes.rationale: aiService.js must call OpenAI only from the backend, never expose the key to the frontend, and return a rule-based fallback explanation when the key is missing.

nodes.label: Phase 12 - Environment Variables
nodes.rationale: server/.env.example centralizes all optional provider credentials so the app runs safely with blank keys; real keys must never be committed.

nodes.label: Phase 13 - Frontend API Connection
nodes.rationale: Frontend must call backend routes, display pricing source (mock vs live), display warnings, and show AI explanation source.

nodes.label: Phase 14 - Vite Proxy
nodes.rationale: Vite proxy forwards /api requests from the frontend dev server to the Express backend on port 5000, avoiding CORS issues in development.

nodes.label: Phase 15 - Frontend UX Improvements
nodes.rationale: Improve spacing, cards, labels, loading/warning states while keeping a dark, modern, beginner-friendly design.

nodes.label: Phase 16 - Validation
nodes.rationale: Frontend and backend must validate budget, required fields, and use case, returning friendly errors instead of crashing on messy input.

nodes.label: Phase 17 - README Updates
nodes.rationale: Explicitly instructs creation/update of README.md documenting setup, mock/live pricing, OpenAI explanations, and the browser hardware-scan limitation.

nodes.label: Phase 18 - Root Scripts
nodes.rationale: Optional root package.json with dev:client/dev:server/build:client/start:server scripts for convenience.

nodes.label: Phase 19 - Testing
nodes.rationale: Manual test checklist covering backend/frontend startup, form submission, auto-fill, mock warnings, and graceful failure when backend is down.

nodes.label: POST /api/analyze
nodes.rationale: Considers budget, use case, missing fields, RAM, storage type, and missing CPU/GPU to determine bottleneck and recommended upgrade path.

nodes.label: mockPricingProvider.js
nodes.rationale: Ensures the app works without any real API keys by supplying demo pricing data as the default PRICING_PROVIDER.

nodes.label: amazonCreatorsProvider.js
nodes.rationale: Amazon PA-API is deprecated, so this provider is placeholder scaffolding only and must not be required for the MVP.

nodes.label: System Info Paste Parser
nodes.rationale: Browsers cannot automatically scan a user's PC for privacy/security reasons, so BuildBetter uses a safe paste-based Windows System Information parser instead of live hardware scanning.

nodes.label: React Compiler (not enabled)
nodes.rationale: Not enabled in this template due to its impact on dev and build performance.
